key_insight: A weakly supervised deep learning model (MIMIC) can help triage early-stage mycosis fungoides versus benign inflammatory dermatoses on histology, with high sensitivity at a safety-focused threshold.
clinical_relevance: This could reduce unnecessary ancillary testing and speed up review of difficult skin biopsies while preserving near-complete detection of classic MF.
method: Trained on 3,339 whole-slide images from two Dutch centres using weakly supervised attention-based multiple-instance learning.
Externally validated on 371 slides from four independent European centres.
Compared morphology-only performance against 11 pathologists in a blinded reader study and then tested clinical utility in a held-out consecutive cohort.
evidence_signal: In external and clinical utility evaluation, the model achieved AUROCs around 0.84-0.91, and in the held-out cohort it reached 97.8% sensitivity with 50.2% specificity at the 0.04 threshold.
watch_item: Performance may vary across centres and case mix, so real-world deployment needs local validation, careful threshold setting, and workflow integration before use.
paper_title: Histological triage of early-stage mycosis fungoides using a weakly supervised deep learning-based model: a multicentre, external validation, and clinical utility study
